name: Vidyard
subcategory: screen recording, walkthroughs and product demos
tagline: Record personalized sales videos and organize them locally for manual sending

pricing.notes: Common Starter monthly amount; vendor packaging changes frequently.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 5 recordings/month; 30-minute recording maximum; 15 AI videos; 3 custom AI avatars; no video hosting

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: Unlimited recordings and recording length; full analytics; branded pages; CTAs; password protection; folders
tiers.notes: Billed annually at $59/seat/month; a 14-day trial is offered.

tiers.name: Teams
tiers.limits: Custom pricing for teams, positioned for 5+ users; CRM/MAP integrations and advanced analytics

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom seats, integrations, API, permissions, SSO and security

pricing.freeTierCaps: 5 recordings/month, 30 minutes maximum each, 15 AI videos and 3 custom AI avatars; no video hosting
pricing.billingTerms: Starter is annual credit-card billing; Teams and Enterprise are annual or multi-year invoiced contracts
pricing.hiddenCosts: Unlimited AI-video workflows require the separately priced Video Agent add-on; caption translations on Teams/Enterprise are billed per minute.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Vidyard, record personalized sales videos and organize them locally for manual sending. The hard boundary is video hosting, viewer identity, crm integrations, team analytics, and sales workflows, plus capture polish, hosting, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Record personalized sales videos by capturing a screen or window with microphone audio, trim and annotate key moments, organize the files locally, and export shareable videos for manual sending.
whatYouLose: video hosting, viewer identity, CRM integrations, team analytics, and sales workflows
ongoingBurden: OS permissions, codecs, rendering performance, uploads, storage, links, and viewer analytics
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Vidyard because the recording itself is easy; the subscription removes upload, transcoding, sharing, organization, and support work. The recurring cost buys OS permissions, codecs, rendering performance, uploads, storage, links, and viewer analytics, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Cap
priorArt.desc: Open-source screen recording and sharing product with modern desktop architecture.

alternatives.name: Cap
alternatives.desc: Record screen and camera, keep an organized library, then paste the link into your own sales email.

alternatives.name: Screenity
alternatives.desc: Unlimited screen-and-camera recording with local or Drive output; personalization is still manual, as requested.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a personal desktop recorder DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Vidyard in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, ffmpeg, and SQLite; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: record personalized sales videos by capturing a screen or window with microphone audio, trim and annotate key moments, organize the files locally, and export shareable videos for manual sending.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Offer screen, window, or region capture plus optional microphone audio.
Show an always-visible recording timer and make stop available from the tray.
Create a non-destructive trim view with crop, zoom, cursor highlight, and text callouts.
Render locally through ffmpeg with sensible H.264 and WebM presets.
Generate a poster frame, transcript, and Markdown summary beside each video.
Provide copy-file-path and reveal-in-folder actions instead of mandatory cloud upload.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out public cloud hosting.
Deliberately leave out viewer identity and engagement analytics.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workspaces and SSO.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
